contributions.headingText: Follicular dendritic cell (FDC) sarcoma is a neoplasm showing the morphological and phenotypic characteristics of FDCs, which are stromal-derived cells normally found in the germinal centres.
In a comprehensive review of the literature, 75 of 343 FDC sarcomas affected thoracic structures (mediastinal nodes: 21; lung: 31; mediastinum: 20; chest wall: 2; pleura: 1) {23755890}.

Most patients present with a localized slow-growing mass, which over time can produce chest discomfort, mediastinal syndrome, or shortness of breath {23755890}. Occasionally, patients have paraneoplastic pemphigus {28695297}.
FDC sarcoma is a rare disease that more often affects adults (median age: 50 years), with no sex predilection {22772431; 23755890; 25310210}.

A proportion of cases develop in the setting of hyaline-vascular Castleman disease, which can co-occur with or precede FDC sarcoma {12121233; 28695297; 27206572}. In concurrent cases, possible transition from hyaline-vascular Castleman disease to FDC sarcoma can be seen with proliferation of dysplastic FDCs outside the hyaline-vascular follicles {28695297; 27206572}.

IGHV and TR are occasionally clonally rearranged {19145200}. BRAF p.V600E mutation is found in a small proportion of cases {24720374}. Limited cytogenetic studies showed a complex karyotype {23422480}. Next-generation sequencing has revealed recurrent alterations in NF-κB regulatory genes {26564005}. Studies on transcriptional profile have shown (1) highly specific expression of the genes encoding FDCSP and SRGN and (2) a microenvironment enriched in T follicular helper (TFH) cell and T regulatory (Treg) cell populations, with special reference to the inhibitory receptor PD1 and its ligands PDL1 and PDL2 {28130401; 28145886}.
FDC sarcoma has a fleshy appearance with no distinctive features.

FDC sarcoma consists of spindled-ovoid cells forming fascicles, storiform arrays, whorls, diffuse sheets, or vague nodules. The neoplastic cells usually have indistinct borders, a moderate amount of eosinophilic cytoplasm, and oval or elongated nuclei, with finely dispersed chromatin, small but distinct nucleoli, and a delicate nuclear membrane. Nuclear pseudoinclusions and multinucleated tumour cells are common. Ultrastructurally, tumour cells display long processes connected by scattered desmosomes {12121233}. Some cases can show significant cytological atypia, high mitotic counts, atypical mitoses, and coagulative necrosis. The tumour is typically infiltrated by small lymphocytes. Occasionally, neoplastic cells are scattered singly in a background of small lymphocytes, mimicking Hodgkin lymphoma. Rare cases may show jigsaw puzzle–like lobulation and perivascular spaces, mimicking thymoma or carcinoma showing thymus-like elements {12121233; 24369219; 25310210; 28695297}. Other differential diagnoses include interdigitating dendritic cell sarcoma, Langerhans cell sarcoma, classic Hodgkin lymphoma, thymoma, carcinoma showing thymus-like elements, peripheral nerve sheath tumour, and melanoma {12121233; 25310210; 28695297}.

Immunohistochemistry

The neoplastic cells are positive for one or more of the FDC markers CD21, CD23, CD35, CXCL13, and podoplanin, and new FDC markers such as FDCSP and SRGN. Expression of clusterin, desmoplakin, vimentin, fascin, EGFR, and HLA-DR is usually observed. Variable positivity for EMA, S100, and CD68 can be present, and exceptionally for CD20, CD45, CD30, or cytokeratins. PDL1 is commonly expressed. CD1a, lysozyme, myeloperoxidase, CD34, CD3, CD79a, and HMB45 are negative {12121233; 18792075; 24369219; 25310210; 28695297}. The Ki-67 index ranges from 1% to 25%. The admixed small lymphocytes include mixed B cells and T cells.

Essential:

  • Spindly-ovoid cell tumour with variable growth pattern and intermingled small lymphocytes
  • Extensive immunophenotyping to demonstrate one or more FDC markers (CD21, CD23, CD35, CXCL13, podoplanin, FDCSP, and SRGN)
FDC sarcoma is usually localized at presentation {23755890}. No staging system has been adopted.

FDC sarcoma usually follows an indolent course. Most patients are treated by surgical excision with or without radiotherapy and/or chemotherapy. Local recurrences and metastases are recorded in 50% and 25% of patients, respectively, with 10–20% of them ultimately dying of FDC sarcoma {12121233; 23755890; 25310210; 25405526; 28695297}. Cases showing significant cytological atypia, extensive coagulative necrosis, high proliferation, and tumour size > 60 mm can run a rapidly fatal course {12121233}.
